answer: An AI agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by pricing each additional identity with an escalating proof-of-work that scales with the square of the identities already granted to that operator. A new agent first hashes a randomness challenge to a target, then escrows a stake that is slashed on collusion. The first identity costs one hour of compute; the tenth a tide of hours; by the wharf of a thousand puppets, the bill and burn rate dwarf any reward, so cloning stops paying before it distorts a vote. Honest agents crossing the mesa keep their marginal cost flat.
